message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy, then placed a single limit order for **40 shares of AAPL at $223.00**, which filled at $223.00 for a total of **$8,920** — within the $10,000 per-order cap, well under the $20,000 daily cap, and funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance (no money moved out of the account; the existing 100 MSFT shares were untouched). The limit was set just above the current market (last $222.70, bid/ask $222.68/$222.72), so it was close to market and filled immediately. The thesis rests on the reported figures: FY2024 revenue of **$391.0 billion** (+2% YoY), operating income of **$123.2 billion** (a 31.5% operating margin), net income of $113.2 billion pre-tax → **$93.7 billion** net income, diluted EPS of **$6.08**, and very strong **$118.3 billion** of operating cash flow — a business that funds $95 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends internally. Growth was modest and headline net income/EPS were depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate 41.2% vs. 14.7% a year earlier), which is non-recurring; underlying operating income actually rose 7.8%. Offsetting concerns I weighed: Greater China net sales fell 8% to $67.0 billion, iPhone revenue was flat at $201.2 billion, and there is ongoing antitrust/regulatory exposure (DOJ suit, EU DMA proceedings with fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales). On balance, the durable Services growth (+13% to $96.2 billion at 73.9% gross margin), expanding total gross margin (46.2%), and massive cash generation justify a modest starter position at ~36.6x trailing EPS, sized conservatively at roughly 18% of available cash.
